preamble: The alveolar trill [r] loses its apical vibration and is realized as a voiced retroflex (postalveolar) fricative [ʐ]: when the tongue tip fails to make contact, the high-velocity airflow of the trill produces continuous frication. This assibilated /r/ is a hallmark of Andean Spanish, where the trill (spelled rr, or r word-initially) is commonly pronounced [ʐ] in highland Bolivia and northern Ecuador. A similar pattern is reported for word-initial /r/ in Chicahuaxtla Triqui (Mixtecan), where the trill is less common than fricative realizations.

examples.note: In a reading corpus of words such as these from 8 speakers in the Bolivian highlands, 574 of 750 tokens of the trill phoneme /r/ were realized as the retroflex fricative [ʐ], 154 as alveolar [z], and only 22 as a fricative trill [r̝] or a trill [r].
Acoustic data from urban and rural dialects show extensive use of [ʐ] for /r/; Spanish loans with /r/ in Imbabura Quichua and Media Lengua are likewise adapted with [ʐ].

Word-initial <r> was formerly described as a trill [r], but it is more commonly pronounced with frication, as voiced [ʐ] or voiceless [ʂ]; only some speakers keep the trill. Elliott et al. (2016) therefore analyse the phoneme as /ʐ/.
